claims: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II marks the first crewed flight to the Moon in over half a century.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission is testing the Orion spacecraft.
The Artemis II mission includes four astronauts.
The Artemis II astronauts include the first woman and first Black person to go to the Moon.
The Artemis II mission travels around the lunar far side.
The Artemis II mission lifted off on a Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Artemis II mission lifted off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B.
The Artemis II crew consists of Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialists Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA).
The Artemis II crew will travel around the far side of the moon.
The Artemis II crew will reach unprecedented distances.
On day 6 of the Artemis II mission, the crew will pass over the lunar south pole.
On day 6 of the Artemis II mission, the crew will witness a total solar eclipse from the far side.
The Artemis II mission includes testing life support systems.
The Artemis II mission includes radiation monitoring.
The Artemis II mission includes deploying international satellites.
